sources.title: aws/aws-graviton-getting-started README
sources.excerpt: This repository provides technical guidance for users and developers using [Amazon EC2 instances powered by AWS Graviton processors](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/graviton/) (including the latest generation Graviton5 processors). While it calls out specific features of the Graviton processors themselves, this repository is also generally useful for anyone running code on Arm-based systems.
sources.limitations: Processor architecture, documented family names and software guidance only. Does not establish all regional availability, pricing, training workloads, suppliers or company-wide hardware portfolio.

sources.title: Broadcom-Network-Switching-Software/OpenBCM README
sources.excerpt:
This release has support for XGS switch devices such as Trident (TD2, TD3, TD4), Tomahawk (TH, TH2, TH3)
and DNX devices such as Ramon, Qumran (Q2A, Q2U) and Jericho (JR2, J2C).
sources.limitations: Documents OpenBCM support for the named switch devices; does not establish the complete/latest Tomahawk portfolio, commercial availability, customer deployments, InfiniBand, DPU or optical-DSP functionality.

additionalExcerpts.excerpt:
OpenBCM Broadcom Switch Software Development Kit contains the source code for Broadcom network switch APIs 
and drivers for programming Broadcom network switch silicon based platforms.

sources.title: NVIDIA-AI-IOT/jetson-generative-ai-playground README
sources.excerpt: The NVIDIA Jetson AI Lab is your guide to running generative AI models entirely on-device with NVIDIA Jetson. Explore optimized tutorials, benchmarks, and hands-on examples for LLMs, VLMs, image generation, speech recognition, and more.
sources.limitations: Documents Jetson as on-device hardware for AI and the associated tutorial site. Does not establish each product module, production model deployments, NPU architecture, AI-PC positioning, quantities or current commercial availability.

changes.description: AWS Graviton is a family of Arm-based processors used in Amazon EC2 instances. AWS publishes technical guidance for its documented processor generations and for building, migrating and optimizing software on Graviton.
changes.provides: Arm-based server processors powering Amazon EC2 instance families.
changes.howUsed: Applications run on Graviton-powered EC2 instances using Arm-compatible software; AWS documents compiler options, operating systems, containers and workload optimization.

type.scope: Classify the explicitly documented processor family as hardware technology, not a separate company. This is atlas taxonomy, not a legal-status finding.

description.scope: Processor family and technical-guide scope only.

products.scope: Named processor generations in the inspected AWS technical-guide table; not an exhaustive historical portfolio or a guarantee of access in every region.

provides.scope: Arm architecture and use in EC2 established by the guide; no training/customer/supplier claim.

howUsed.scope: Software migration/build/deployment guidance described in the guide.

website.scope: Product URL linked from the AWS technical guide; destination was not separately retrieved.

notes: Corrects the generic x86 / Arm server CPU / RISC-V bundle with the exact families documented in AWS guidance. Retain original data in Git history.
Does not add or remove any entity, nor infer Annapurna ownership or an accelerator training relationship.

productFacts.name: Graviton processor family
productFacts.description: Arm-based processors used in EC2; the inspected guide lists Graviton2, Graviton3(E), Graviton4 and Graviton5.
productFacts.scope: Architecture and documented family identities only; exact instance region, pricing and lifecycle require separate evidence.

changes.description: Broadcom Tomahawk is a family of network-switch devices. Broadcom documents support for TH, TH2 and TH3 devices in its OpenBCM switch software development kit.
products: Tomahawk switch devices (TH / TH2 / TH3 documented in OpenBCM)
changes.provides: Network-switch silicon programmable through Broadcom OpenBCM APIs and drivers.
changes.howUsed: System software uses Broadcom switch APIs and drivers to program supported Tomahawk switch devices.

type.scope: The source identifies Tomahawk as network-switch devices, supporting a hardware-technology record rather than a company record.

description.scope: OpenBCM device support; not a complete or latest Tomahawk product-generation census.

products.scope: Only the TH / TH2 / TH3 device names explicitly listed by this OpenBCM release. This is a scoped documented subset.

provides.scope: Network-switch devices supported by OpenBCM; no unsupported generic InfiniBand/DPU/Optics DSP attribution.

howUsed.scope: OpenBCM describes APIs and drivers for programming network-switch silicon.

website.scope: Primary vendor software documentation for this scoped device-support claim.

notes: Replaces the unsourced generic Ethernet / InfiniBand / DPU / Optics DSP portfolio with the narrow documented switch-device family.
Does not assert that TH3 is the latest generation. Other generations require their own sources.
No customer, deployment, throughput, current shipment or ownership claim established.

changes.description: NVIDIA Jetson is hardware for running AI models on-device. NVIDIA Jetson AI Lab publishes tutorials, benchmarks and examples for local language, vision-language, image-generation and speech-recognition workloads.
changes.provides: On-device AI hardware and documented model-deployment examples through Jetson AI Lab.
changes.howUsed: Developers follow Jetson AI Lab tutorials to run supported AI workloads on local Jetson hardware.

type.scope: Source explicitly describes Jetson hardware; hardware technology is the appropriate atlas class rather than an independent company.

description.scope: On-device AI hardware and tutorial coverage described by the README; not proof of production deployment or all module capabilities.

provides.scope: Jetson hardware and the documented AI Lab example scope only.

howUsed.scope: Documented tutorial use; no performance or universal model-compatibility promise.

website.scope: Documentation site linked by the inspected NVIDIA project.

notes: Existing generic Edge accelerator / AI PC / Embedded NPU tags are not substantiated by this source. Keep them visibly unreviewed unless separately corrected.
No release date, price, module inventory, NPU architecture, supplier or customer claim established.
